chapter_note: A highly systematic substrate teaching about cosmic pre-ordination/foreknowledge of the light. Seven moments follow a uniform pattern: 'Before [condition], [cosmic agent] was [prepared].' The structure is self-evidently complete and architectonic. Only ¶1 (dialogue frame) and ¶5 (editorial bridge inserting 'the sects' into the cosmic pattern) fall outside the oldest layer. Teaching purity is very high (0.913). The moderate institutional drift in the second half is minimal, concentrated in ¶5. The chapter preserves a remarkably intact substrate teaching about emanation sequence and cosmic determinism.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic session opening: 'Once again, hear this other lesson that I would teach you!' First-person address to audience with no cosmological content. Standard compilation frame marker.

paragraphs.core_text: Before night and day were differentiated in the universe, the Third [Am]bassador was summoned. And afterwards, he was sent to this void and outer waste that he might purify the light, and separate night and day from each other.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Know that' — pedagogical address marker (minor frame element directing audience attention).
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Know that' is a borderline case — it exists in Persian pedagogical tradition but is an audience-address formula. The cosmological content is pure substrate: Ambassador as cosmic agent, night/day differentiation, purification of light, void/outer waste as cosmic geography. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.117⟩ Before the light was released and freed and ascended through this zone, the Father of Life made beautiful for it the ships of light. He constructed them so that it might be purified in them, and be sculpted and fashioned in good order.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Father of Life → cosmic agent. Ships of light → cosmic vessels. Zone → cosmic geography. Light purification, sculpting, fashioning → cosmic process vocabulary. High substrate score (13.64). Both sides internal to cosmic system. The vocabulary of crafting/construction (sculpted, fashioned, constructed) maps emanation as architectural act.

paragraphs.core_text: [Bef]ore Sin had multiplied and had made a kingdom in the flesh, before the acquitted and the condemn[ed] were set apart from each other, the Judge [w]as sent forth and revealed. His throne was created and placed [i]n the living atmosphere, so that he would be a just Judge, so that there the righteous and the sinners would be set apart and tested and separated from each other.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Sin personified as cosmic agent ('had multiplied and had made a kingdom') — capitalized per extraction rules. Judge → cosmic agent. Throne → cosmic seat. Living atmosphere → cosmic geography. The separating/testing function is cosmic process, not ethical exhortation. 'Acquitted and condemned' and 'righteous and sinners' function as cosmic categories (light/dark mixture being separated), not contemporary moral application.

Editorial extension mimicking the substrate 'Before X, Y was prepared' pattern but reaching outside the cosmic system. 'The sects' are contemporary religious groups in the editor's world — the ONLY paragraph where one side of the mapping leaves the cosmic architecture. 'The blessed Christ' uses honorific ('blessed') absent from the impersonal substrate voice. Institutional vocabulary score (6.45) confirms. If removed, the seven-moment teaching remains structurally complete with six cosmic stages (Ambassador → ships → Judge → stars/zodiac → destroyers → Builder).

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [befo]re mankind had been engendered, some were named ['rich' and] others 'poor' on earth [ ... ] upon them. ⟨p.118⟩ Before they die, they who will die are marked out by the stars and the signs of the zodiac in the sphere. They are appointed for them; in them are their births. And their root is bound up with their zodiacal signs; and they are compelled by them and brought to an equal judgement in accordance with their deeds and their sins.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Astral determinism teaching — stars, zodiac, sphere are cosmic geography. 'Their root is bound up with their zodiacal signs' is a classic body-cosmos correspondence (root/zodiac binding formula). 'Rich'/'poor' function as cosmic fate categories determined by astral configuration, not social commentary. 'In accordance with their deeds and their sins' is cosmic mechanism (karmic process within the astral system), not moral exhortation. Lacuna [...] preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, before the universe is dissolved, [and the] entire earth, the destroyers were appointed and instructed for its dissolution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Cosmic eschatology — destroyers as cosmic agents appointed for dissolution of the universe. Both sides internal to cosmic system. Brief but structurally essential as the penultimate stage in the pre-ordination sequence.

paragraphs.core_text: And before the ne[w] aeon was [built and] made be[auti]ful and marked out, [the] Great Builder [w]as summoned, the first architect and the angels who are with him, who would build and make beautiful the new aeon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate with highest substrate score in chapter (21.62). Great Builder / first architect → cosmic agents. New aeon → cosmic geography/eschatology. 'Build and make beautiful' echoes the crafting vocabulary of ¶3 (Father of Life 'made beautiful' the ships). The structural closure: from pre-cosmic summoning (¶2, Ambassador) to post-cosmic construction (¶8, Builder). Multiple restorations from manuscript damage preserved.
